requirements.summary: Review and acceptance specifications for the work-item CRUD endpoints implementation in FastAPI.
acceptance_criteria: POST /work-items accepts title and optional description, stores the item in the database, and returns HTTP 201 with the created work item (id, title, description, status, created_at).
GET /work-items retrieves all existing work items ordered by ID descending and returns HTTP 200 with the item list.
PATCH /work-items/{item_id} updates the status of an existing work item, returning HTTP 200 with the updated item details, or HTTP 404 if the item ID does not exist.
DELETE /work-items/{item_id} removes the work item from the database, returning HTTP 200 with confirmation, or HTTP 404 if the item ID does not exist.
Database connection failures and SQL execution exceptions across all work-item endpoints are caught and return HTTP 500 with a detailed error message.

architecture.summary: The route handlers violate separation of concerns by embedding raw SQL and direct connection management inside main.py without connection pooling or response contracts.
findings: Separation of concerns: Database operations and raw SQL queries are implemented directly within FastAPI route handlers in main.py instead of being decoupled into a repository or data access layer (e.g. expanding src/app/db.py).

Connection management: Each request opens and closes a new database connection via psycopg.connect(settings.database_url). This introduces high latency and risks connection exhaustion under load; a connection pool (e.g., psycopg_pool) or shared connection lifecycle should be utilized.

Information disclosure in error handling: Catching generic exceptions and returning f'Database error: {exc}' in HTTP 500 responses exposes internal database implementation details, connection states, and SQL errors to API consumers.
API contracts: Endpoints return ad-hoc dictionary structures instead of defining typed Pydantic response models (e.g., WorkItemResponse) with response_model annotations on the routes.

qa_security.summary: QA and security review flagged several vulnerabilities and reliability issues including information disclosure via unhandled exception leakage, risk of connection exhaustion DoS from unpooled database connections, and lack of bounded input validation.
security_risks: Information disclosure: raw exception details are directly interpolated into HTTP error responses (e.g., detail=f'database unavailable: {exc}'), leaking internal database schemas and network topologies.

Denial of Service (DoS) / Connection exhaustion: establishing a new direct database connection per request without connection pooling risks exhausting database connection limits under moderate traffic.
Unbounded input validation: WorkItemCreate allows arbitrarily large strings for title and description without length constraints or sanitization, presenting memory and storage exhaustion risks.
